sanskrit: rathasaṃghāṃs tathā nāgān hayāṃś ca saha sādibhiḥ pādātāṃś ca susaṃkruddhaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ amṛdnāt samare rājan saṃpradhāvaṃs tatas tataḥ
english: Chariot-hosts and elephants, horses together with their riders, and foot-soldiers too, the enraged warrior crushed by hundreds and by thousands, O king, charging this way and that across the battlefield.

sanskrit: tena saṃloḍyamānaṃ tu pāṇḍūnāṃ tad balaṃ mahat saṃcukoca mahārāja carmevāgnau samāhitam
english: Churned and harried by him, that great host of the Pāṇḍavas shrank back, O great king, like a hide drawn tight in the fire.

sanskrit: bhagnaṃ tu svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagadattena dhīmatā ghaṭotkaco 'tha saṃkruddho bhagadattam upādravat
english: Seeing his own host broken by the wise Bhagadatta, Ghaṭotkaca then, filled with wrath, rushed upon Bhagadatta.

sanskrit: vikaṭaḥ puruṣo rājan dīptāsyo dīptalocanaḥ rūpaṃ vibhīṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā roṣeṇa prajvalann iva
english: A fearsome figure, O king, with blazing face and blazing eyes, assuming a terrifying form, he seemed to flame with fury.

sanskrit: jagrāha vipulaṃ śūlaṃ girīṇām api dāraṇam nāgaṃ jighāṃsuḥ sahasā cikṣepa ca mahābalaḥ saviṣphuliṅgajvālābhiḥ samantāt pariveṣṭitam
english: He seized a massive spear that could rend even mountains, and, eager to slay the elephant, the mighty one suddenly hurled it, wreathed all around with sparks and flames.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā dṛṣṭvā jvālākulaṃ raṇe cikṣepa ruciraṃ tīkṣṇam ardhacandraṃ sa pārthivaḥ ciccheda sumahac chūlaṃ tena bāṇena vegavat
english: Seeing it rushing suddenly upon him in the fray, wreathed in flame, that king loosed a bright, keen crescent-headed arrow and with that swift shaft cleft the enormous spear in two.

sanskrit: nipapāta dvidhā chinnaṃ śūlaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam mahāśanir yathā bhraṣṭā śakramuktā nabhogatā
english: Cut in two, the gold-adorned spear fell, like a great thunderbolt loosed by Śakra and hurtling fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: śūlaṃ nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā dvidhā kṛttaṃ sa pārthivaḥ rukmadaṇḍāṃ mahāśaktiṃ jagrāhāgniśikhopamām cikṣepa tāṃ rākṣasasya tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Seeing the spear fallen, cleft in two, that king took up a great dart with a golden shaft, like a tongue of fire, and hurled it at the rākṣasa, crying, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ saṃprekṣya viyatsthām aśanīm iva utpatya rākṣasas tūrṇaṃ jagrāha ca nanāda ca
english: Beholding it rushing down upon him like a thunderbolt poised in the sky, the rākṣasa leapt up at once, caught it, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: babhañja caināṃ tvarito jānuny āropya bhārata paśyataḥ pārthivendrasya tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And swiftly, setting it upon his knee, he broke it, O Bhārata, before the very eyes of that lord of kings; a marvel, it seemed, came to pass.

sanskrit: tad avekṣya kṛtaṃ karma rākṣasena balīyasā divi devāḥ sagandharvā munayaś cāpi vismitāḥ
english: Beholding that deed done by the mighty rākṣasa, the gods in heaven, with the gandharvas and the sages, were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca maheṣvāsā bhīmasenapurogamāḥ sādhu sādhv iti nādena pṛthivīm anunādayan
english: And the Pāṇḍava great archers, with Bhīmasena at their head, made the earth resound with the cry, "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: taṃ tu śrutvā mahānādaṃ prahṛṣṭānāṃ mahātmanām nāmṛṣyata maheṣvāso bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān
english: But hearing that great shout of the exultant high-souled ones, the great archer Bhagadatta, full of valor, could not bear it.

sanskrit: sa visphārya mahac cāpam indrāśanisamasvanam abhidudrāva vegena pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathān visṛjan vimalāṃs tīkṣṇān nārācāñ jvalanaprabhān
english: Drawing his great bow, whose twang was like the roar of Indra's thunderbolt, he rushed with speed upon the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, loosing bright, keen iron shafts that gleamed like flame.

sanskrit: bhīmam ekena vivyādha rākṣasaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ abhimanyuṃ tribhiś caiva kekayān pañcabhis tathā
english: He pierced Bhīma with one arrow, the rākṣasa with nine shafts, Abhimanyu with three, and the Kekayas with five.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena svarṇapuṅkhena patriṇā bibheda dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ kṣatradevasya cāhave papāta sahasā tasya saśaraṃ dhanur uttamam
english: With a winged, golden-nocked shaft loosed from a fully drawn bow, he pierced the right arm of Kṣatradeva in the battle, and suddenly his excellent bow, with its arrow, fell from his grasp.

sanskrit: draupadeyāṃs tataḥ pañca pañcabhiḥ samatāḍayat bhīmasenasya ca krodhān nijaghāna turaṃgamān
english: Then he struck the five sons of Draupadī with five arrows, and in his wrath he slew the horses of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: dhvajaṃ kesariṇaṃ cāsya ciccheda viśikhais tribhiḥ nirbibheda tribhiś cānyaiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya patribhiḥ
english: He cut down his lion-bannered standard with three barbless shafts, and with three other winged arrows he pierced through his charioteer.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopastha upāviśat viśoko bharataśreṣṭha bhagadattena saṃyuge
english: Deeply wounded and stricken, Viśoka sank down upon the chariot-seat, O best of the Bhāratas, struck by Bhagadatta in the fight.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahārāja viratho rathināṃ varaḥ gadāṃ pragṛhya vegena pracaskanda mahārathāt
english: Then Bhīma, O great king, that foremost of chariot-warriors, now bereft of his chariot, seized his mace and sprang swiftly down from the great car.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā saśṛṅgam iva parvatam tāvakānāṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ samapadyata bhārata
english: Seeing him with mace upraised, like a mountain with its peak, a dreadful terror came upon your warriors, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu pāṇḍavaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ ājagāma mahārāja nighnañ śatrūn sahasraśaḥ
english: At that very moment, O great king, the Pāṇḍava whose charioteer was Kṛṣṇa came up, slaying his foes by the thousand.

sanskrit: yatra tau puruṣavyāghrau pitāputrau paraṃtapau prāgjyotiṣeṇa saṃsaktau bhīmasenaghaṭotkacau
english: He came to where those two tigers among men, father and son, scorchers of the foe, Bhīmasena and Ghaṭotkaca, were locked in struggle with the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavo rājan yudhyamānān mahārathān tvarito bharataśreṣṭha tatrāyād vikirañ śarān
english: Seeing those great chariot-warriors locked in combat, O king, the Pāṇḍava, O best of the Bhāratas, came there in haste, scattering his shafts.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā tvaramāṇo mahārathaḥ senām acodayat kṣipraṃ rathanāgāśvasaṃkulām
english: Then King Duryodhana, that great chariot-warrior, in his haste swiftly urged on his host, thronged with chariots, elephants, and horses.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā kauravāṇāṃ mahācamūm abhidudrāva vegena pāṇḍavaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Against that great Kaurava army rushing suddenly upon him, the Pāṇḍava borne by white horses charged with speed.

sanskrit: bhagadatto 'pi samare tena nāgena bhārata vimṛdnan pāṇḍavabalaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: Bhagadatta too in the battle, O Bhārata, crushing the Pāṇḍava host with that elephant, rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tadāsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhagadattasya māriṣa pāñcālaiḥ sṛñjayaiś caiva kekayaiś codyatāyudhaiḥ
english: Then there was a tumultuous battle, O honored sir, between Bhagadatta and the Pāñcālas, the Sṛñjayas, and the Kekayas with weapons upraised.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi samare tāv ubhau keśavārjunau āśrāvayad yathāvṛttam irāvad vadham uttamam
english: And Bhīmasena in the battle made both Keśava and Arjuna hear, just as it had happened, of the grievous slaying of Irāvat.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca putraṃ tu nihataṃ śrutvā irāvantaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭo niḥśvasan pannago yathā
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing that his son Irāvat had been slain, Dhanaṃjaya, overcome with great grief, hissed like a serpent.

sanskrit: abravīt samare rājan vāsudevam idaṃ vacaḥ idaṃ nūnaṃ mahāprājño viduro dṛṣṭavān purā
english: In the midst of the battle, O king, he spoke these words to Vāsudeva: "Surely it was this that the deeply wise Vidura foresaw of old—

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca kṣayaṃ ghoraṃ mahāmatiḥ tato nivārayitavān dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram
english: the terrible destruction of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas; and so that great-minded one strove to restrain Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men.

sanskrit: avadhyā bahavo vīrāḥ saṃgrāme madhusūdana nihatāḥ kauravaiḥ saṃkhye tathāsmābhiś ca te hatāḥ
english: Many heroes who ought never to have been slain, O slayer of Madhu, have been struck down in this battle by the Kauravas, and slain by us as well.

sanskrit: arthahetor naraśreṣṭha kriyate karma kutsitam dhig arthān yatkṛte hy evaṃ kriyate jñātisaṃkṣayaḥ
english: For the sake of wealth, O best of men, this contemptible deed is done. Cursed be that wealth, for whose sake such a destruction of kinsmen is wrought!

sanskrit: adhanasya mṛtaṃ śreyo na ca jñātivadhād dhanam kiṃ nu prāpsyāmahe kṛṣṇa hatvā jñātīn samāgatān
english: Better death in poverty than wealth won by the slaying of kin. What shall we gain, O Kṛṣṇa, by slaying our kinsmen gathered here?

sanskrit: duryodhanāparādhena śakuneḥ saubalasya ca kṣatriyā nidhanaṃ yānti karṇadurmantritena ca
english: Through the offense of Duryodhana, of Śakuni the son of Subala, and through the evil counsel of Karṇa, the kṣatriyas go to their destruction.

sanskrit: idānīṃ ca vijānāmi sukṛtaṃ madhusūdana kṛtaṃ rājñā mahābāho yācatā sma suyodhanam rājyārdhaṃ pañca vā grāmān nākārṣīt sa ca durmatiḥ
english: And now I understand, O slayer of Madhu, how rightly the king acted, O mighty-armed one, when he begged of Suyodhana but half the kingdom, or even five villages—yet that evil-minded one would not grant it.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā hi kṣatriyāñ śūrāñ śayānān dharaṇītale nindāmi bhṛśam ātmānaṃ dhig astu kṣatrajīvikām
english: For seeing the valiant kṣatriyas lying upon the face of the earth, I bitterly reproach myself: a curse upon the warrior's calling!

sanskrit: aśaktam iti mām ete jñāsyanti kṣatriyā raṇe yuddhaṃ mamaibhirucitaṃ jñātibhir madhusūdana
english: These kṣatriyas will think me powerless in battle. Yet for me, O slayer of Madhu, this warring against my own kinsmen is no fit thing.

sanskrit: saṃcodaya hayān kṣipraṃ dhārtarāṣṭracamūṃ prati pratariṣye mahāpāraṃ bhujābhyāṃ samarodadhim nāyaṃ klībayituṃ kālo vidyate mādhava kva cit
english: Drive the horses swiftly toward the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son. With my two arms I shall cross to the far shore of this vast ocean of war. This, O Mādhava, is no time anywhere for faintness of heart.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena keśavaḥ paravīrahā codayām āsa tān aśvān pāṇḍurān vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, Keśava, slayer of enemy heroes, urged on those white horses, swift as the wind.

sanskrit: atha śabdo mahān āsīt tava sainyasya bhārata mārutoddhūtavegasya sāgarasyeva parvaṇi
english: Then a great roar arose from your army, O Bhārata, like that of the ocean swelling at the full moon, lashed to fury by the wind.

sanskrit: aparāhṇe mahārāja saṃgrāmaḥ samapadyata parjanyasamanirghoṣo bhīṣmasya saha pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: In the afternoon, O great king, a battle joined between Bhīṣma and the Pāṇḍavas, with a din like that of the storm-cloud.

sanskrit: tato rājaṃs tava sutā bhīmasenam upādravan parivārya raṇe droṇaṃ vasavo vāsavaṃ yathā
english: Then, O king, your sons rushed upon Bhīmasena, surrounding Droṇa in the fray as the Vasus surround Vāsava.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ kṛpaś ca rathināṃ varaḥ bhagadattaḥ suśarmā ca dhanaṃjayam upādravan
english: Then Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, and Kṛpa that best of chariot-warriors, and Bhagadatta and Suśarman rushed upon Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: hārdikyo bāhlikaś caiva sātyakiṃ samabhidrutau ambaṣṭhakas tu nṛpatir abhimanyum avārayat
english: Hārdikya and Bāhlika both rushed upon Sātyaki, while the king Ambaṣṭhaka held off Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: śeṣās tv anye mahārāja śeṣān eva mahārathān tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayāvaham
english: The rest of the great chariot-warriors, O great king, engaged the rest in turn; and so there began a battle, dreadful of aspect, fraught with terror.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃprekṣya putrāṃs tava janeśvara prajajvāla raṇe kruddho haviṣā havyavāḍ iva
english: But Bhīmasena, beholding your sons, O lord of men, blazed up in the battle in his wrath, like the fire that bears the oblation fed with ghee.

sanskrit: putrās tu tava kaunteyaṃ chādayāṃ cakrire śaraiḥ prāvṛṣīva mahārāja jaladāḥ parvataṃ yathā
english: And your sons covered the son of Kuntī with their arrows, O great king, as the rain-clouds in the wet season veil a mountain.

sanskrit: sa cchādyamāno bahudhā putrais tava viśāṃ pate sṛkkiṇī vilihan vīraḥ śārdūla iva darpitaḥ
english: Covered on every side by your sons, O lord of the people, that hero licked the corners of his mouth, like a tiger swollen with pride.

sanskrit: vyūḍhoraskaṃ tato bhīmaḥ pātayām āsa pārthiva kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena so 'bhavad gatajīvitaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, O king, with a keen razor-headed shaft, brought down Vyūḍhoraska, and he was bereft of life.

sanskrit: apareṇa tu bhallena pītena niśitena ca apātayat kuṇḍalinaṃ siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: And with another broad-headed shaft, yellow and whetted sharp, he struck down Kuṇḍalin, as a lion brings down a lesser beast.

sanskrit: tataḥ suniśitān pītān samādatta śilīmukhān sa sapta tvarayā yuktaḥ putrāṃs te prāpya māriṣa
english: Then, swiftly, he took up seven well-whetted yellow shafts, O honored sir, when he had come upon your sons.

sanskrit: preṣitā bhīmasenena śarās te dṛḍhadhanvanā apātayanta putrāṃs te rathebhyaḥ sumahārathān
english: Those arrows, sped by Bhīmasena of the firm bow, struck down your sons, mighty chariot-warriors, from their cars.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣṭiṃ kuṇḍabhedaṃ vairāṭaṃ dīrghalocanam dīrghabāhuṃ subāhuṃ ca tathaiva kanakadhvajam
english: Anādhṛṣṭi, Kuṇḍabheda, Vairāṭa, Dīrghalocana, Dīrghabāhu, Subāhu, and likewise Kanakadhvaja—

sanskrit: prapatanta sma te vīrā virejur bharatarṣabha vasante puṣpaśabalāś cūtāḥ prapatitā iva
english: those heroes, as they fell, shone forth, O bull of the Bhāratas, like mango trees in spring, dappled with blossoms, brought down to the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradudruvuḥ śeṣāḥ putrās tava viśāṃ pate taṃ kālam iva manyanto bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: Then the rest of your sons fled away, O lord of the people, deeming the mighty Bhīmasena to be Death itself.

sanskrit: droṇas tu samare vīraṃ nirdahantaṃ sutāṃs tava yathādriṃ vāridhārābhiḥ samantād vyakirac charaiḥ
english: But Droṇa, as that hero was consuming your sons in the battle, showered him on every side with arrows, as a mountain is drenched by streams of rain.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma kuntīputrasya pauruṣam droṇena vāryamāṇo 'pi nijaghne yat sutāṃs tava
english: There we beheld the marvelous prowess of the son of Kuntī, for though held back by Droṇa, he still went on slaying your sons.

sanskrit: yathā hi govṛṣo varṣaṃ saṃdhārayati khāt patat bhīmas tathā droṇamuktaṃ śaravarṣam adīdharat
english: As a mighty bull endures the rain falling from the sky, so Bhīma bore up under the shower of arrows loosed by Droṇa.

sanskrit: adbhutaṃ ca mahārāja tatra cakre vṛkodaraḥ yat putrāṃs te 'vadhīt saṃkhye droṇaṃ caiva nyayodhayat
english: And a wondrous deed, O great king, did Vṛkodara perform there, for he slew your sons in battle and fought with Droṇa as well.

sanskrit: putreṣu tava vīreṣu cikrīḍārjunapūrvajaḥ mṛgeṣv iva mahārāja caran vyāghro mahābalaḥ
english: Among your heroic sons the elder brother of Arjuna sported, O great king, ranging like a mighty tiger among deer.

sanskrit: yathā vā paśumadhyastho drāvayeta paśūn vṛkaḥ vṛkodaras tava sutāṃs tathā vyadrāvayad raṇe
english: And as a wolf in the midst of a herd would scatter the beasts, so Vṛkodara scattered your sons in the battle.

sanskrit: gāṅgeyo bhagadattaś ca gautamaś ca mahārathaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe vārayām āsur arjunam
english: The son of Gaṅgā, and Bhagadatta, and Gautama that great chariot-warrior held off in the fight the impetuous Pāṇḍava Arjuna.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya teṣāṃ so 'tiratho raṇe pravīrāṃs tava sainyeṣu preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: Warding off their missiles with his own, that surpassing chariot-warrior in the battle sent the chief heroes of your armies to their death.

sanskrit: abhimanyuś ca rājānam ambaṣṭhaṃ lokaviśrutam virathaṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kārayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: And Abhimanyu with his shafts made the king Ambaṣṭha, renowned through the world, that best of chariot-warriors, bereft of his car.

sanskrit: viratho vadhyamānaḥ sa saubhadreṇa yaśasvinā avaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ savrīḍo manujādhipaḥ
english: Bereft of his chariot and hard-pressed by the illustrious son of Subhadrā, that lord of men, in shame, swiftly leapt down from his car.

sanskrit: asiṃ cikṣepa samare saubhadrasya mahātmanaḥ āruroha rathaṃ caiva hārdikyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: He hurled his sword in the battle at the high-souled son of Subhadrā, and then mounted the chariot of the high-souled Hārdikya.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ tu nistriṃśaṃ yuddhamārgaviśāradaḥ lāghavād vyaṃsayām āsa saubhadraḥ paravīrahā
english: But the son of Subhadrā, slayer of enemy heroes, skilled in the ways of war, by his nimbleness made that flying sword miss its mark.

sanskrit: vyaṃsitaṃ vīkṣya nistriṃśaṃ saubhadreṇa raṇe tadā sādhu sādhv iti sainyānāṃ praṇādo 'bhūd viśāṃ pate
english: Seeing the sword turned aside by the son of Subhadrā in the battle, then a great cry of "Well done! Well done!" arose from the armies, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhās tv anye tava sainyam ayodhayan tathaiva tāvakāḥ sarve pāṇḍusainyam ayodhayan
english: The others, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, fought against your army, and in the same way all your warriors fought against the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tatrākrando mahān āsīt tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata nighnatāṃ bhṛśam anyonyaṃ kurvatāṃ karma duṣkaram
english: There arose a great clamor among yours and among theirs, O Bhārata, as they smote one another fiercely and wrought deeds hard to do.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ hi raṇe śūrāḥ keśeṣv ākṣipya māriṣa nakhair dantair ayudhyanta muṣṭibhir jānubhis tathā
english: For the warriors in the battle, O honored sir, seizing one another by the hair, fought with nails, with teeth, with fists, and with knees.

sanskrit: bāhubhiś ca talaiś caiva nistriṃśaiś ca susaṃśitaiḥ vivaraṃ prāpya cānyonyam anayan yamasādanam
english: And with arms, and with open palms, and with well-whetted swords, finding an opening, they sent one another to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: nyahanac ca pitā putraṃ putraś ca pitaraṃ raṇe vyākulīkṛtasaṃkalpā yuyudhus tatra mānavāḥ
english: Father slew son and son slew father in the battle; their purpose utterly distracted, the men fought there.

sanskrit: raṇe cārūṇi cāpāni hemapṛṣṭhāni bhārata hatānām apaviddhāni kalāpāś ca mahādhanāḥ
english: In the battle, O Bhārata, beautiful bows with golden backs, flung from the hands of the slain, and costly quivers lay scattered.

sanskrit: jātarūpamayaiḥ puṅkhai rājataiś ca śitāḥ śarāḥ tailadhautā vyarājanta nirmuktabhujagopamāḥ
english: Sharpened arrows, with nocks of gold and silver, washed with oil, gleamed forth like serpents that had cast their skins.

sanskrit: hastidantatsarūn khaḍgāñ jātarūpapariṣkṛtān carmāṇi cāpaviddhāni rukmapṛṣṭhāni dhanvinām
english: Swords with hilts of ivory, adorned with gold, and shields with golden backs, flung away from the bowmen, lay strewn about.

sanskrit: suvarṇavikṛtaprāsān paṭṭiśān hemabhūṣitān jātarūpamayāś carṣṭīḥ śaktyaś ca kanakojjvalāḥ
english: Barbed darts wrought with gold, pikes adorned with gold, lances all of gold, and spears bright with the gleam of gold,

sanskrit: apakṛttāś ca patitā musalāni gurūṇi ca parighān paṭṭiśāṃś caiva bhiṇḍipālāṃś ca māriṣa
english: all cut down and fallen, lay there—and heavy maces, and iron clubs, and pikes, and slings too, O honored sir.
